story_type: night rocket launch from pad cameras, lunar lander that later tipped over on the Moon
hook: This rocket was sending a lander to the Moon's south pole.
narration: This rocket was sending a lander to the Moon's south pole.
A Falcon 9 lifted off from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy at seven sixteen at night, February twenty-sixth, 2025.
On top was Athena, a lander from Intuitive Machines, carrying NASA science and a drill.
The nine engines light first, and clamps hold the rocket down for a moment while computers check every one.
Then the clamps let go, and the steam cloud swallowed the pad.
Trackers followed the flame as it climbed into the night.
Long-range cameras watched the engines burn far downrange.
[short pause] Eight days later, Athena reached the Moon.
outcome: On March sixth it touched down in a crater near the south pole, on its side, and the mission ended early.
title: Night launch to the Moon's south pole
description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 launches Intuitive Machines' IM-2 lander, Athena, from Kennedy Space Center on Feb. 26, 2025, seen from NASA's pad and tracking cameras. On March 6 it landed on its side in a crater near the lunar south pole.

facts.claim: Falcon 9 carrying IM-2 launched 7:16 p.m. EST Feb. 26 from LC-39A
facts.source_quote: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying Intuitive Machines’ Nova-C lunar lander (IM-2) launches at 7:16 p.m. EST on Wednesday, Feb. 26 from Launch Complex 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center
The Nova-C lander, named Athena, captured and transmitted images of the landing site before activating the technology and science instruments.

facts.claim: Carried a drill and other instruments; landed on its side
facts.source_quote: confirmed the lander was on its side, preventing it from fully operating the drill and other instruments before its batteries were depleted.

facts.claim: Touched down March 6 in a crater near the South Pole
facts.source_quote: IM-2 touched down at approximately 11:30 a.m. March 6
calling an early end of mission at 12:15 a.m. CST Friday

extra_sources.excerpt: The Nova-C lander, named Athena, captured and transmitted images of the landing site before activating the technology and science instruments. ... Intuitive Machines said images collected later confirmed the lander was on its side, preventing it from fully operating the drill and other instruments before its batteries were depleted. ... IM-2 touched down at approximately 11:30 a.m. March 6 ... touching down inside a crater on the Moon ... calling an early end of mission at 12:15 a.m. CST Friday
